title: Adaptive phase-split scheduler for prefill/decode to balance tail latency and throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The runtime currently uses either static phase-splitting (fixed prefill:decode token budget) or simple heuristics for prefill/decode scheduling. This leads to two classes of issues: 1) short, low-token interactive requests (chat turns, few-token replies) experience high tail decode latency when prefill-heavy batches monopolize GPUs; 2) dynamic workload shifts (sudden long-prefill bursts) can starve decode work and violate latency SLOs for premium customers.

Proposal: Implement an adaptive phase-split scheduler that dynamically adjusts prefill vs decode share per GPU pool and per scheduling lane. The scheduler will be workload-aware and SLO-driven: it observes short-term statistics (queue lengths, seq-length histograms, in-flight KV cache hit rate, recent p95/p99 latency for decode and prefill) and computes a target phase split using a small control loop. The goal is to protect tail latency for latency-sensitive traffic while preserving overall throughput and cost efficiency.

Key ideas: compute token-budget quotas, apply per-tenant or per-route weighting for fairness, gradual throttling of prefill when decode latency breaches thresholds, and a fallback policy that routes overflow prefill to lower-cost pools instead of blocking decode. The algorithm supports both soft and hard splits and can operate in two modes: global per-GPU and per-route adaptive modes.

Why this is different: rather than enforcing a fixed phase boundary or a single fairshare algorithm, this scheduler reacts to real-time signals and explicitly optimizes a configurable objective (latency SLOs + throughput target), enabling fine-grained trade-offs and safer rollouts for Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler is feature-flagged and can be enabled per-cluster and per-route
p95 decode latency for short requests (<= 32 tokens) improves by >= 20% in synthetic mixed workloads without degradation of overall token throughput by > 5%
No increase in token cost per 1k requests (within measurement noise) for targeted workloads
Canary rollout completed: 5% of production traffic for 48h with dashboards and alerting
Integration tests for fairness heuristics and stress tests for extreme prefill bursts are added to CI
comments: 2025-02-11 - Initial design sketched in sync with Runtime team. We need histograms of seq-length per-route (Marco). Action: add telemetry event for per-request token counts (Aisha)

2025-02-12 - Reviewed fairness options. PM suggests per-customer weighting rather than strict round-robin to avoid penalizing heavy paying customers. Note: this requires tying scheduler input to billing tiers (product will provide mapping).

2025-02-14 - Prototype experiment: local simulator produced promising results: p95 decode down 28% on mixed 70/30 prefill-heavy workload while throughput dropped 3%. Simulator code: github.com/redwood/runtime-scheduler/sim/tree/eng-9270 (WIP PR 142)

2025-02-17 - Design review with Observability: need new metrics (decode_share_target, scheduling_decisions, prefill_throttle_events). Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/4Q8ph/scheduler-923
2025-02-19 - Security review flagged possible information leak in per-tenant telemetry; we will anonymize customer IDs before publishing aggregated histograms. Security ticket: SEC-2101

2025-02-20 - Implementation notes: Rust runtime change set 2314 touches scheduler.rs and batch_coordinator. Will add feature flag runtime.scheduler.adaptive_phase_split and a canary config by cluster.
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument telemetry: per-request token counts, decode/prefill queue lengths, per-route latency percentiles. 2) Build a lightweight controller that computes target decode_share per lane every 100-500ms using exponentially-weighted moving averages. 3) Integrate controller with batch_coordinator: apply soft token quotas and a fallback routing policy. 4) Add canary flag and per-cluster rollout, expose config in Console. 5) Run mixed-workload canaries, gather p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost metrics, iterate on control parameters.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Oscillation when control loop reacts too aggressively. Mitigation: use damping, capped rate of change, and require sustained threshold breaches before hard throttling. Risk: fairness regressions for large tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant weights and canary validation against billing tiers. Risk: telemetry cost and cardinality. Mitigation: aggregate histograms and downsample events.
related_work: ENG-4821 (scheduling fairness vs throughput), ENG-7312 (prefill/decode fairshare policy), research notes from 2024 infra week on KV cache-aware batching.
next_steps: 1) Marco to land telemetry PR by 2025-02-25. 2) Aisha to land simulator improvements and finalize control law by 2025-02-27. 3) Begin runtime implementation once telemetry is live. 4) Schedule canary for 2025-03-03.
notes: Keep algorithm parameterizable in Console (latency_slo_ms, min_decode_share, max_prefill_throttle_pct). Aim for safe defaults to avoid customer impact when enabled accidentally.
